newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin seeks economic policy outline next week.
newsitem.headline: Jospin seeks economic policy outline next week.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin told parliament on Thursday he was asking Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn to present the outlines of his new left-wing government's economic policy next week.
In a keynote address, he said that he said that an audit of public finances would be ready in July, paving the way to a mini-budget in the autumn.

Jospin said he was asking Strauss-Kahn to contact the finance commissions in the National Assembly and the Senate "to present, next week, the first outlines of the government's economic and financial policies."

Jospin said he would not present a mini-budget immediately because the results of a planned audit of public finances, that will enable France to see how close it is to meeting criteria for a single European currency, would only be ready in mid-July.
"The financial measures that the government will be led to undertake will be presented to parliament in the autumn mini-budget," he said.
